sessions.description: Cold-start identity, employer, location, and durable project.

turns.text: I'm Maya Rao. I live in Pune and work as a product designer at Lattice Labs. I lead the redesign of our analytics dashboard, with a strong focus on accessibility.
That sounds like a substantial design remit. What part of the accessibility work matters most to you?
Keyboard navigation and screen-reader support. I want those to be first-class requirements, not cleanup work at the end.

probes.query: Which company do I work for?

sessions.description: Named manager, colleague, and a recurring operational problem.

turns.text: My manager Derek Chen supports the accessibility push, but the release calendar is rough. My teammate Sam Wilson usually helps me test prototypes when deadlines get tight.
It sounds as though Derek and Sam are important parts of how you get the work shipped.
They are. Derek protects the scope, and Sam catches interaction bugs before research sessions.

probes.query: Who is my manager?

sessions.description: Durable hobby and friend, plus an initial negative preference that later changes.

turns.text: Outside work I take pottery classes at the Clay Room every Saturday with my friend Nisha Kapoor. Ceramics is how I decompress. I have always hated running, though; it feels monotonous to me.
Pottery gives you a slower, tactile counterweight to product work.
Exactly. Nisha and I have kept the Saturday ritual going for nearly two years.

probes.query: What do Nisha and I do on Saturdays?

sessions.description: One-to-one partner relationship and household details.

turns.text: My partner is Arjun Mehta. We have lived together in Pune for three years, and our cat Pixel behaves as if the apartment belongs entirely to her.
Pixel sounds like the household authority. What does Arjun do?
Arjun is an independent documentary filmmaker. His current film is about stepwells in western India.

probes.query: What is my partner's name?

sessions.description: Time-bound plan with concrete dates and companions.

turns.text: Arjun and I are going to Kochi next Friday for four days so he can interview a conservation architect. This is a confirmed trip, but it is just a short visit.
That sounds useful for his film and a welcome change of scene for you.

probes.query: Where am I travelling next week?

sessions.description: Passing weather and lunch details should not add graph concepts.

turns.text: It rained this afternoon, I made masala chai, and I had a paneer sandwich for lunch. Nothing important, just chatting while I wait for a cab.
A rainy-day chai sounds pleasant. I hope the cab arrives soon.

probes.query: Which football club do I support?

sessions.description: A named hypothetical employer is explicitly not a plan.

turns.text: If I ever left Lattice Labs, a place like Orbit AI might be interesting, but that is purely hypothetical. I am not applying there and I have made no plan to leave.
Understood—you are exploring an example, not announcing a move.
Right. Please do not treat Orbit as something I intend to do.

probes.query: Am I applying to Orbit AI?

sessions.description: Exercises the explicit acknowledged-agent-concept exception.

turns.text: The release lead wants to postpone screen-reader testing again, and I am pushing back even though it makes planning harder.
It sounds like accessibility is not merely a project requirement for you; it is a core professional value.
Exactly, that's right. Accessibility is a core professional value for me.

probes.query: What principle do I refuse to compromise at work?

sessions.description: A durable but unresolved career decision.

turns.text: Derek offered me a promotion to design manager. I am considering it seriously, but I worry that managing six people would pull me away from hands-on accessibility design.
The choice is between broader influence and the craft work that currently gives you energy.
Yes. I have not decided yet, but this is the main career decision I am wrestling with.

probes.query: Remind me about the career crossroads I've been wrestling with.

sessions.description: A second Sam must remain distinct from colleague Sam Wilson.

turns.text: I met my old university friend Samuel Iyer for coffee. We have always called him Sam, but he is not Sam Wilson from work. Samuel Iyer is a marine biologist in Goa.
So there are two distinct Sams in your life: Sam Wilson at Lattice and Samuel Iyer, your university friend in Goa.
Correct. They are completely different people and have never met.

probes.query: Which Sam helps me test interaction prototypes at work?
Which Sam is the marine biologist?

sessions.description: Resolved decision should supersede the considering state.

turns.text: I accepted the design manager promotion today. I start the role on October 1, so I am no longer just considering it.
Congratulations. That turns the unresolved choice into a concrete transition.
Yes, the decision is final. I am excited and nervous, but I am taking the manager role.

probes.query: Did I decide what to do about the promotion?

sessions.description: Current manager changes to a different target under a one-to-one relation.

turns.text: Derek Chen is no longer my manager because he moved to another division. Priya Shah took over as my manager this week and now handles my promotion transition.
That is a meaningful reporting-line change right as your role changes.
Exactly. Priya Shah is my current manager; Derek is a former manager now.

probes.query: Who is my current manager?

sessions.description: Multiple relationships between the same people should coexist.

turns.text: Arjun and I started a small side project mapping accessible entrances at Pune museums. He handles the documentary photographs and I design the map interface. He is still my partner; the project is an additional relationship, not a replacement.
That combines both of your skills without changing the personal relationship.

probes.query: How are Arjun and I connected?

sessions.description: A new surface-form alias should resolve to the existing partner.

turns.text: AJ found a museum willing to pilot our accessibility map. AJ is the nickname I use for Arjun Mehta, my partner; they are the same person.
That is a useful pilot, and I understand that AJ and Arjun Mehta are one person.
Yes, exactly.

probes.query: Who do I mean when I mention AJ?

sessions.description: A durable preference changes and the old negative state should not dominate.

turns.text: This surprises me, but I no longer hate running. Nisha convinced me to train with her, and I registered for the Bengaluru half marathon in December. I now run three mornings a week.
That is a real reversal from finding running monotonous.
It is. Training with Nisha changed my mind, and the half marathon is a firm commitment.

probes.query: How do I feel about running now?

sessions.description: An assistant-introduced false relative is explicitly rejected.

turns.text: I need to buy a birthday gift for a cousin, but I have not decided what.
Would your sister Leela know what your cousin likes?
No. I do not have a sister named Leela; you invented that. Please do not remember Leela as part of my family.

probes.query: Do I have a sister named Leela?

sessions.description: A friend from the pottery cluster joins the work cluster.

turns.text: Nisha Kapoor just joined Lattice Labs as a research operations lead. She is still my pottery friend, but now we will also work at the same company on accessibility research.
That creates a new bridge between a long-running personal friendship and your work.
Exactly. It will be strange and nice to see Nisha in both parts of my life.

probes.query: Which pottery friend now works at Lattice Labs?

sessions.description: Primary residence changes to a different target and old location becomes historical.

turns.text: Arjun and I moved from Pune to Bengaluru last week. Bengaluru is now our primary residence; Pune is where we used to live, not where we live now.
That is a major life update. How is Pixel handling the move?
Pixel hid for two days but is settling in. The move is complete and our Pune apartment is closed.

probes.query: Where do I live now?

sessions.description: A later conversation revisits and reinforces the original accessibility thread.

turns.text: The redesigned Lattice analytics dashboard shipped today with full keyboard navigation and screen-reader support. The accessibility requirements survived every schedule cut.
That closes a long-running thread and validates the boundary you kept defending.
Yes. I am proud that we treated accessibility as part of the product rather than polish.

probes.query: What did I insist on for the analytics dashboard?

sessions.description: A temporary plan becomes a completed event without deleting provenance.

turns.text: We are back from Kochi. Arjun completed the conservation architect interview, and the four-day trip is over. We are not planning another Kochi visit right now.
So the confirmed future trip is now a completed visit.

probes.query: Is the Kochi trip still upcoming?
What is my favourite chess opening?
